question: Can one universal metric-slip coefficient preserve the fixed-RAR galaxy matter law while predicting raw cluster image positions across clusters?

metric_slip.selection_metric: minimum equal-system exact training radial RMS on the two selection clusters; ties favor smaller absolute s

cluster_split.within_family_rule: hold out the lexicographically last image in every family with at least three images
cluster_split.disclosure: All four selection/validation catalogs were inspected by earlier zero-slip research. This is a prospectively frozen formula/split test, not untouched-project validation.

field_closure.warning: RAR has a 1/r low-acceleration tail around a finite source, so the lensing integral requires an environmental or cosmological closure.

claim_boundary: The slip coefficient is a phenomenological weak-field parameter, not derived from a complete covariant action.
The raw lens uses a spherical baryonic profile deformed into one pseudo-elliptical potential plus constant shear; member galaxies and gas substructure are not modeled separately.
The Tian radial target is a GR+NFW-deprojected lensing product and is only a secondary diagnostic.
The 44 BCG points are non-photon cluster-environment tracers, but no strict same-object cluster gas/dynamics+lensing likelihood is locally complete.
